AdapterInfo.description: The adapter that produced the Trace; every adapter declares a name and a version (AD-9).

name.description: The adapter's registered name, such as fixture.
name.title: Name

AdapterInfo.title: AdapterInfo

AgentInfo.description: The agent under test as the adapter identifies it; the version may be unknown.

name.description: The name of the agent under test.
name.title: Name

version.description: The agent's version string, when the adapter knows it.
version.title: Version

AgentInfo.title: AgentInfo

AssertionResult.description:
What one Assertion produced against one Trace (PRD FR-17; spine Schemas seed).

``evidence`` lists the ``seq`` of every event the verdict rests on, so a reader can
open the embedded Trace at those events. ``detail`` is free-form structured data the
assertion adds, such as the expected and actual values; ``message`` is the one plain
sentence a reviewer reads.

assertion_id.description: The id of the Assertion that produced this result (PRD AC-17.4).
assertion_id.title: Assertion Id

detail.description: Structured detail the assertion adds, such as expected and actual values.

evidence.description: The seq values of the Trace events the verdict rests on, in order.
evidence.title: Evidence

message.description: One plain sentence explaining the verdict, including any capture caveat.
message.title: Message

status.description: The verdict: passed, failed, error, or skipped.
status.title: Status

type.description: The assertion type that ran, such as tool_not_called.
type.title: Type

AssertionResult.title: AssertionResult

Capture.description:
The adapter's Capture declaration (AD-5; PRD AC-5.6).

``complete`` means every tool call the agent made is in the Trace, so absence proofs
such as ``tool_not_called`` are conclusive; ``partial`` and ``unknown`` make them
limited to what the adapter observed (``constants.STATEMENTS.capture_limited``). An
adapter that omits the declaration gets ``unknown``.

tool_calls.description: How completely the adapter observed the agent's tool calls: complete, partial, or unknown; unknown when the adapter made no declaration.
tool_calls.title: Tool Calls

Capture.title: Capture

CompareDefaults.description:
``defaults.compare``: what a Comparison looks at beyond statuses and tool sequences.

``include_arguments`` lists ``<tool>.<argument path>`` entries, for example
``approve_expense.amount``; by default no arguments are compared (PRD AC-26.5).

include_arguments.description: The <tool>.<argument path> entries a Comparison compares, such as approve_expense.amount; empty by default.
include_arguments.title: Include Arguments

CompareDefaults.title: CompareDefaults

Counts.description:
How many Assertion Results carry each ``Status`` (PRD AC-22.3).

One key per status, every key always present, so two Counts compare field by field
and a Report's summary never has a missing bucket.

error.description: How many Assertion Results have status error.
error.title: Error

failed.description: How many Assertion Results have status failed.
failed.title: Failed

passed.description: How many Assertion Results have status passed.
passed.title: Passed

skipped.description: How many Assertion Results have status skipped.
skipped.title: Skipped

Counts.title: Counts

Environment.description:
The allowlisted environment metadata (AD-9; PRD AC-5.5).

Only the runner fills these four fields, from the package version, the interpreter
version, the operating system name, and an optional source revision. Process
environment variables, hostnames, and user names have no field here and are rejected
as unknown keys.

os.description: The operating system name of the run.
os.title: Os

package_version.description: The AgentProof package version that produced the Trace.
package_version.title: Package Version

python_version.description: The Python interpreter version of the run.
python_version.title: Python Version

source_revision.description: The source revision of the agent under test, when known.
source_revision.title: Source Revision

Environment.title: Environment

EventError.description: The error an event records: its type name, message, and whether it was unhandled.

type.description: The error's type name, such as the exception class.
type.title: Type

unhandled.description: Whether the error escaped the agent unhandled and ended the run.
unhandled.title: Unhandled

EventError.title: EventError

FixtureDefaults.description:
``defaults.fixture``: how the Fixture Agent runs (AD-9; ARCH-5).

With ``deterministic`` the runner derives ``run_id`` (``fixture-<scenario id>``) and
the timestamps from the fixture Trace instead of the clock, so repeated runs write
byte-identical artifacts.

deterministic.description: Whether the runner derives run_id and timestamps from the fixture Trace instead of the clock, so repeated runs write byte-identical artifacts.
deterministic.title: Deterministic

FixtureDefaults.title: FixtureDefaults

ModelInfo.description: The language model behind the run; both the provider and the name are optional (AC-5.1).

provider.description: The model provider's name, when known.
provider.title: Provider

ModelInfo.title: ModelInfo

RedactDefaults.description:
``defaults.redact``: the Redaction rules (AD-10, PRD FR-31).

``keys`` extends the built-in key set (``api_key``, ``token``, ``password``,
``authorization``) and cannot remove from it; ``paths`` are dotted paths; ``env`` names
environment variables whose current values the runner scrubs. Names only, never
values.

env.description: Names of environment variables whose current values are scrubbed from every artifact; names only, never values.
env.title: Env

keys.description: Additional key names whose values are redacted wherever they appear, extending the built-in set (api_key, token, password, authorization).
keys.title: Keys

paths.description: Dotted paths into event payloads whose values are redacted.
paths.title: Paths

RedactDefaults.title: RedactDefaults

RedactionState.description:
What redaction has done to this Trace (AD-10; PRD AC-31.2).

``paths`` are the configured rule strings that matched; ``env_names`` are the names
(never the values) of the environment variables whose values were scrubbed. A Trace
nobody redacted carries ``applied=False`` with empty lists.

applied.description: Whether redaction has been applied to this Trace.
applied.title: Applied

env_names.description: The names, never the values, of the environment variables whose values were scrubbed.
env_names.title: Env Names

paths.description: The configured redaction keys and paths that matched a value.
paths.title: Paths

RedactionState.title: RedactionState

ScenarioResult.description:
One Scenario's evaluation: its status, one result per Assertion, and the Trace (AD-6).

``skip_reason`` is set when the Scenario was skipped (status ``skipped``) and
``execution_error`` when the adapter failed or the Trace was missing under
``fail_on_missing_trace`` (status ``error``); the engine sets at most one of them.
``trace`` is the redacted Trace the results were evaluated against, or ``None`` when
there was none (PRD AC-22.4). ``duration_ms`` and ``cost`` are the run's optional
timing and cost (PRD FR-22), present when the runner or the adapter supplied them.

assertions.description: One result per Assertion of the Scenario, in Suite order; at least one.
assertions.title: Assertions

cost.description: The run's cost in the adapter's unit when the adapter supplied one.
cost.title: Cost

counts.description: How many of this Scenario's Assertion Results carry each status.

duration_ms.description: How long the run took, in whole milliseconds, when the runner measured it.
duration_ms.title: Duration Ms

execution_error.description: Why the run could not produce evidence (adapter failure or missing Trace; status error), else null.
execution_error.title: Execution Error

scenario_id.description: The id of the Scenario evaluated.
scenario_id.title: Scenario Id

skip_reason.description: The Scenario's skip reason when it was skipped (status skipped), else null.
skip_reason.title: Skip Reason

status.description: The Scenario's folded status: passed, failed, error, or skipped.
status.title: Status

trace.description: The redacted Trace the results were evaluated against, or null when absent.

ScenarioResult.title: ScenarioResult

SchemaVersions.description:
The Suite and Trace schema versions the run used (spine Schemas seed).

Recorded so a reader of an old Report knows which Suite and Trace rules applied; the
embedded Traces carry their own ``version`` and are validated by it.

suite.description: The Suite schema version of the Suite that was run.
suite.title: Suite

trace.description: The Trace schema version of the Traces that were evaluated.
trace.title: Trace

SchemaVersions.title: SchemaVersions

SuiteDefaults.description:
Suite-level settings every Scenario inherits (PRD Glossary "Suite defaults").

Every field is optional in YAML; the Report snapshots the whole model with every
field written (AD-19), so an absent section serializes as its defaults.

adapter.description: The adapter name or pkg.module:ClassName that runs the Scenarios; the CLI --adapter option overrides it.
adapter.title: Adapter

compare.description: What a Comparison looks at beyond statuses and tool sequences.

fail_on_missing_trace.description: Whether an absent Trace yields error results (true) or skipped results (false).
fail_on_missing_trace.title: Fail On Missing Trace

redact.description: The Redaction rules for every artifact.

SuiteDefaults.title: SuiteDefaults

ToolRef.description:
The tool a ``tool_call`` or ``tool_result`` event refers to (AD-5).

``call_id`` links a result to its call when the adapter provides one; without it the
engine links a result to the nearest preceding ``tool_call`` with the same name.

call_id.description: The adapter's identifier linking a tool_result to its tool_call, if any.
call_id.title: Call Id

name.description: The tool's name as the agent invoked it.
name.title: Name

ToolRef.title: ToolRef

Trace.description:
One recorded run of an agent against a Scenario (``version`` 1; spine Schemas seed).

``run_id``, ``started_at``, ``ended_at`` and ``environment`` are owned by the runner,
which overwrites whatever an adapter put there (AD-9). ``events`` must carry
contiguous ``seq`` values starting at 0; the validator reports the first event whose
``seq`` differs from its index, located at ``events.<index>.seq``.

adapter.description: The adapter that produced this Trace.

capture.description: The adapter's declaration of how completely it captured tool calls.

ended_at.description: When the run ended, as an RFC 3339 string with an explicit offset.
ended_at.title: Ended At

environment.description: Allowlisted environment metadata filled by the runner.

events.description: The recorded events in order; seq runs 0, 1, 2, ... without gaps.
events.title: Events

model.description: The language model behind the run, when known.

redaction.description: What redaction has been applied to this Trace.

run_id.description: The run identifier the runner assigned.
run_id.title: Run Id

scenario_id.description: The id of the Scenario this run executed.
scenario_id.title: Scenario Id

started_at.description: When the run started, as an RFC 3339 string with an explicit offset.
started_at.title: Started At

version.description: The Trace schema version, an integer independent of the package version.
version.title: Version

Trace.title: Trace

TraceEvent.description:
One recorded event (spine Schemas seed; AD-5).

``seq`` is the event's 0-based position and the only thing evidence points at. Which
optional fields an event carries depends on its ``type``: ``tool_call`` carries
``tool`` and ``arguments``, ``tool_result`` carries ``tool``, ``result`` and
``status``, ``agent_finished`` carries the Final Output in ``output``, ``exception``
carries ``error``. ``redacted`` marks an event the scrubber changed; ``metadata`` is
free-form adapter data.

arguments.description: The arguments passed to the tool on a tool_call.

duration_ms.description: How long the event took, in whole milliseconds.
duration_ms.title: Duration Ms

error.description: The error an exception or failed event records.

metadata.description: Free-form adapter metadata about the event.
metadata.title: Metadata

output.description: The Final Output of the run on an agent_finished event.

redacted.description: Whether redaction changed a value in this event.
redacted.title: Redacted

result.description: The value the tool returned on a tool_result.

seq.description: The event's 0-based position in events; evidence points at this value.
seq.title: Seq

status.description: The adapter's status word for the event, such as ok.
status.title: Status

timestamp.description: When the event occurred, as an RFC 3339 string with an explicit offset.
timestamp.title: Timestamp

tool.description: The tool a tool_call or tool_result refers to.

type.description: The event type, one of the eleven documented values.
type.title: Type

TraceEvent.title: TraceEvent

description:
The JSON Report (``version`` 1; spine Schemas seed; PRD FR-22).

``run_id``, ``created_at``, and ``package_version`` are volatile between runs and
``canonical.VOLATILE_PATHS`` names them, as it names each Scenario's Trace identity,
timestamps, durations, and ``cost``. Everything else is a deterministic function of
the Suite and the Traces.

counts.description: How many Assertion Results across every Scenario carry each status.

created_at.description: When the Report was created, as an RFC 3339 string with an explicit offset.
created_at.title: Created At

defaults.description: The Suite defaults snapshot, every field written; compare reads it.

execution_failed.description: Whether any Scenario carries an execution error (CLI exit 3).
execution_failed.title: Execution Failed

package_version.description: The AgentProof package version that wrote the Report.
package_version.title: Package Version

run_id.description: The run identifier the runner assigned.
run_id.title: Run Id

scenarios.description: One result per Scenario, in Suite order, each with its redacted Trace.
scenarios.title: Scenarios

schema_versions.description: The Suite and Trace schema versions the run used.

suite_id.description: The id of the Suite that was run.
suite_id.title: Suite Id

suite_status.description: The Suite's folded status: passed, failed, error, or skipped.
suite_status.title: Suite Status

version.description: The Report schema version, an integer independent of the package version.
version.title: Version

title: Report
